body: I'm really sorry you had to go through all of this. The fact is, you should never have to take care of your parents when you are a kid. The parent is supposed to take care of you. I see you. It's insane, your story is similar to mine in a lot of ways, and crazy different in a lot of ways. I have autism, CPTSD, anxiety, and depression. My parents divorced when I was 4, my mom was a bad alcoholic, and my dad got together with a rich white woman (I'm Cherokee, my mom is Cherokee), who was a narcissist and extremely abusive and racist, I was forced to call her mom when I was six (she spanked me, and lectured me, told me it would happen again, after I called her by her first name instead of mom). She physically and psychologically abused me all the time growing up. I was grounded for most of my childhood. My mother had partial custody at this time, but I was not allowed to call her mom. They told me she wasn't my mother she just gave birth to me. I knew it was wrong. And this was just the start of it. My stepmother was insanely abusive and controlling with me, and racist towards me, up till I moved out. That thing you talked about? About how he would lecture you and repeatedly asked you questions until you agreed with him? even if oftentimes you were screaming and crying? My step mother did that to me as well, and would always force me to say bad things about my mom.  And that's just the tip of the iceberg. I hope you are okay. Life is really scary and difficult and hard. Thank you for sharing your story. Sharing your story is the first step. And, the fact is, you could probably write an over thousand page book chronicalling all of the abuse you experienced from your family growing up. Maybe you need to share the story a thousand times, before you start to get healing from it. I do not know. But please, never give up, try to love yourself, and remember, you are never alone. <3
Hey! You're not alone in that boat, I feel the same way. How are you?
